title: Recording: Hi, Hi, Hi by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: John Leckie

Wings continued recording the song ‘Hi, Hi, Hi’ on 18 September 1972.

For much of the month they had been vacillating between sweetening a live version recorded in Groningen during the Wings Over Europe Tour in August, and a studio version started on 3 September.

On this day Paul McCartney decided to record a simpler studio version, with a standard rock beat instead of a shuffle rhythm, and power chords from Henry McCullough and Denny Laine.

They recorded 24 takes between 1.30pm and midnight, only 13 of which were complete. Take 24 was selected the best, onto which McCartney overdubbed lead vocals, and McCullough and Laine added lead guitar parts. However, the result were again deemed to be substandard, and the following day McCartney chose to work on take 17 instead.

Paul was just after that magic take, I suppose. “I remember endless shuffling around of sounds. They tried different amps, different guitars and different arrangements: faster, slower. There was no producer; Paul was trying to produce it himself. He’d come up and help me with the sound, so he’d be with me, tweaking sounds. He probably needed a producer for those sessions.
John Leckie, 1 December 2016
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73
